target: false (staminal) corona; no PO term found, so the corona of the stamens (PO: stamen-borne corona, to be added) rather than stamen (PO_0009029)
fix: Comparatives right after an appositive noun phrase ('held in a cup-shaped false corona, much shorter than X') describe that noun phrase, not the subject of the clause.
reason: In Pancratium the stamens are joined into a false corona that is much shorter than the perianth lobes. The corona carries the '2 triangular lobes between the stamens', so 'much shorter' describes the corona, not the free stamens.

target: number of dichotomous branching orders of the stem (count of branching events), not amount of branch
fix: 'N times (dichotomously) branched' gives how many times the stem forks (branching orders). The number of branches is 2^N, not N, so the number must not become a branch count.
reason: 2–3 forkings give about 4–8 branch tips, so 'branch amount 2–3' is false.
Female inflorescences are usually ± simple (unbranched), in contrast to the branched male ones. The female context and 'usually' are both kept.
'Stipules: Absent' is correctly stipule present, negated.
Leaf blade ovate or ovate-cordate. Ovate-cordate (ovate with a cordate base) fits heart shaped well enough, and the base is cordate per the same description.

target: PO_0030102 nut fruit (nutlet; the samara-like fruitlet)
fix: 'nutlet(s)' is a fruit or fruitlet (PO_0030102 has nutlet as a synonym), never a seed.
reason: In Liriodendron the winged units of the aggregate fruit are 1–2-seeded samaroid nutlets. The text even says '1- or 2-seeded', so the wing belongs to the fruitlet, not the seed.

fix: In a corolla with fused petals, 'lobes' after 'corolla … tube' are corolla lobes (FLOPO_0986006), not whole petals.
reason: The free lobes are longer than the corolla tube. A whole petal includes its share of the tube, so the comparison does not hold for the petal.
The lateral nerves (secondary veins) of the blade are 4–6 on each side, and the count position is kept.

target: the bracteoles and sepals together (joint count of perianth-subtending phyllomes), not sepal alone
fix: When a count follows a joined subject ('X and Y N'), the number counts X and Y together. Do not give it to the last noun alone.
reason: In Camellia the bracteoles and sepals grade into each other and are counted together as 7–8(–10). There are fewer sepals than that.
Stamens 10.

target: position: branch leaves (leaf on branch), as distinct from stem leaves
fix: In moss descriptions, 'Branch leaves' and 'Stem leaves' are given separately. The qualifier must be kept as a position or whole slot (leaf of branch).
reason: The length 1.4–1.9 mm is for branch leaves only. Stem leaves in Leucodon are usually larger, so 'leaf length' without the qualifier is too general.
'Sepals abaxially pubescent' becomes sepal abaxial epidermis, pubescent.
Bracts 0.9–1.2 by 0.6–0.7 mm, and the first number is the length.
(0.15–)0.3–0.8(–1.1) dm is correctly (1.5–)3–8(–11) cm. Height of the stem of a scapose herb is acceptable.

target: range from narrowly elliptic-ovate to elliptic-obovate (both ends are compound shapes: ovate–elliptic and obovate–elliptic)
fix: Joined shape words 'X-Y' (elliptic-ovate, ovate-lanceolate) name one in-between shape. The hyphen is not a range connector. Only 'to' joins the ends of a range here.
reason: The relation was read as 'narrowly elliptic' to 'ovate' across the hyphen. The real endpoint 'elliptic-obovate' was lost, so the range is wrong.
The style slightly surpasses (is longer than) the nutlets. The added 'not surpassing prickles' does not make this false.

fix: 'later (often) X' after a description of young material sets a later stage. The stage word 'later' must fill the stage slot.
reason: The leaves are hairy above and on the nerves beneath, and only later become glabrescent or glabrous. Without the stage, the annotation contradicts the earlier 'hairy'.
Anthers 0.5–1 mm.

fix: In a list 'A, A-B, or A-C' each item is a whole shape. Do not split compounds at the hyphen and take only the second part.
reason: The relation 'lanceolate, or elliptic' drops 'ovate' and cuts the compounds down to their second parts. 'Lanceolate' alone and 'elliptic' alone are not what the flora says.
Achenes ovoid or obovoid. Ovoid fits PATO ovate (ovoid is a synonym) until the pending PATO shape term arrives, and obovoid fits FLOPO_0991025.

target: target whole: base (FLOPO_0985024) of perianth lobe (FLOPO_0986004)
fix: 'inserted at base of X': the target is the base of X. The 'of X' must fill the whole slot of the target, or the target is the base of an unknown part.
reason: The target is only 'base', with no part it belongs to. The insertion point is the base of the perianth lobes, not some other base.
Corolla white or greenish. 'Greenish' fits green.

target: staminal sheath / filament tube (the 'gouttière', the open tube of fused filaments), not stamen
fix: French 'à N [adj.] de …' after a part brings in a new sub-part (gouttière). The adjective belongs to that sub-part, not to the head part.
reason: The membranous part 2.5 mm wide is the open staminal tube (gutter) of the diadelphous androecium, not the stamens as a whole.
The leaflet lobes are (2–)4–8(–10), and the leaflet container is right.
Inflorescence terminal or axillary.

target: FLOPO_0988008 purple (bluish purple is a NARROW synonym of purple)
fix: English two-colour compounds put the main colour last: 'bluish-purple' is a purple, and 'purplish blue' is a blue. Do not swap the main and modifying colour.
reason: The colour synonym table maps 'bluish purple' to purple (FLOPO:0988008), but the annotation used purplish blue (FLOPO_0988026).

fix: 'abaxially X' after a part should become the abaxial surface of that part as the bearer (as in A07061). The side word must not be dropped.
reason: Only the lower (abaxial) side is pale green. The upper side is green, later blue-gray, so 'leaf lamina pale green' is false.
The style is at length (when mature) deciduous. The mature context covers 'at length'.

fix: A more specific bearer exists: PO_0030121 capitulum inflorescence ('capitula' is a synonym).
reason: The capitula are very numerous. A capitulum is an inflorescence, so the statement is true, though PO_0030121 would be more precise.
